data.title: Visual Hierarchy
data.tagline: Visual hierarchy makes visitors read the page in your intended order—headline first, description next, button last.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether "messy" is a hierarchy problem, and direct the AI to assign size, shade, and position by importance.
data.description: Where the eye lands first on a page is not random: size, color, and position steer it. The headline is biggest and boldest so it lands first; the description sits one shade lighter so it reads second; the button carries a fill so it pops last. A page that "looks messy" usually has everything equally large and equally heavy, leaving the eye nowhere to start.

learning.assumes: You have glanced at a poster and could name its headline.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether "messy" is a hierarchy problem, and direct the AI to assign size, shade, and position by importance.

distinctions.label: Typography
distinctions.explanation: Typography governs text alone; Visual Hierarchy steers attention across everything—buttons, images, position included.

distinctions.label: Wireframe
distinctions.explanation: Wireframe arranges which block sits where; Visual Hierarchy decides which of those blocks gets seen first.

explanation.title: Size
explanation.text: More important means bigger. Headline clearly above subtitle, subtitle clearly above body—gaps wide enough to tell apart at a glance.

explanation.title: Shade and fill
explanation.text: Key content in dark ink, secondary one shade lighter; buttons stand out by fill rather than font size.

explanation.title: Position
explanation.text: Higher on the page gets seen sooner—things in the hero are noticed before anything at the bottom.

data.boundary: Hierarchy is not typography—typography governs text size and weight, while hierarchy also covers color, position, and fill. It is not "content order" either: content follows reading logic, hierarchy decides how fast each block gets seen; they cooperate but differ. The diagnostic: squint at the page and check whether the first landing point is the one you wanted.

lessonPractice.title: Visitors say the homepage "has no focus." The title, description, and buttons are nearly the same size. What do you tell the AI?

options.label: Layer by importance: headline clearly larger, description secondary, main button filled
options.feedback: Correct. Widen the gaps (size, color, fill) so the eye travels title → description → button, and the focus emerges on its own.

options.label: Add a big banner at the top saying "the focus is here"
options.feedback: Another same-sized element just joins the fight for attention, adding clutter.

options.label: Shrink all the text so the page feels less crowded
options.feedback: Uniformly smaller text keeps the same ratios—still no order. Crowded and unordered are different problems.

data.agentPrompt: Re-layer the homepage: headline biggest and boldest, description one step smaller and lighter, main button keeps its fill, nothing else competes. Afterward I'll squint at a screenshot—the first thing my eye lands on should be the headline.
